$comment: Q34 — the running topology. What is asserted here is not the technology list but the operational properties: which signal each service scales on, what a rollout does to in-flight work, where the synchronous deadlines are, and which signals are actually watched. A service missing any of those is not operable, whatever it is written in.

messageBridge.purpose: on-premises Oracle SOA queue ↔ cloud topics, so the on-prem path keeps working while services migrate
messageBridge.guarantee: at-least-once, per-aggregate ordering preserved through the bridge

services.name: orders-api

probes.readiness: /health/ready (checks the database and the broker, so traffic only lands on a pod that can serve)

shutdown.behaviour: stop accepting, drain in-flight requests, commit or roll back, then exit

stateInMemory: nothing that must survive a pod: no session, no cache of record

scaling.mechanism: KEDA on consumer lag, not CPU
scaling.rationale: CPU stays low while consumers stall on a slow dependency; lag is the signal that predicts the backlog

consumer.staleMessagePolicy: skip when x-aggregate-version is not greater than the last applied version

shutdown.behaviour: stop fetching, finish the current message, commit or leave unacked, then exit

consumer.replayable: can rebuild the entire projection from topic retention, which is why the payload is a fact and not an instruction

reads.consistency: eventually consistent, lag alerted above 60 s

onPremises.notes: the Oracle SOA / OSB integration is reached through the bridge, not called directly by cloud services

observability.correlationId: injected at the gateway, propagated through every synchronous call and every message header

assumed: the network drops messages and delays them arbitrarily
a consumer will be killed mid-message
a dependency will be slow rather than down, which is the harder case
a clock will disagree between services
notAssumed: a synchronous call that always answers
